question: May a Claw package directly register executable MCP declarations in the global registry, or must those declarations be brokered and scoped to the owning agent or installation?
rationale: The implementation can be made mechanically safer, but only maintainers can decide whether package-install consent is sufficient authority for later host command execution and cross-agent MCP exposure.

options.title: Broker and scope declarations
options.body: Require trusted pinned launchers, sanitized environments, per-agent or per-install names, explicit sharing authorization, and failure compensation before accepting the feature.

options.title: Use bundle-plugin ownership
options.body: Move MCP packaging and trust to the existing bundle-style plugin path and keep Claws limited to referencing approved resources.

options.title: Accept global trusted ownership
options.body: Treat installing a Claw as authorization for global MCP execution and sharing, with the upgrade and sibling-impact contract documented and proven.

recommendation.title: Broker and scope declarations
recommendation.body: Require trusted pinned launchers, sanitized environments, per-agent or per-install names, explicit sharing authorization, and failure compensation before accepting the feature.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned reviewer and the strongest discussion-backed owner of the Claw product and ownership model.
